901dfa97758a486cc35ee9ae25493b1614501bb9: Bödele is a low-key resort on a modest scale — 25 km of runs for an intimate skiing experience, far from the bustle of the big resorts. This is where you come for calm, authenticity and no queues at the lifts. Bödele's reputation as a family resort is well earned: dedicated beginner areas, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for laying the foundations of skiing with children. Bödele's moderate altitude — starting at 700 m and rising to 1,467 m — makes it sensitive to climate variations. January and February remain the most reliable months for optimal snow cover. Outside this window, checking the snow reports before setting off is strongly advised. At 48€, the day lift pass places Bödele among the mid-range resorts on price — neither cheap nor exorbitant. The quality of the ski area and its facilities justifies this price for most skiers. In short: Bödele does not compete with the giants of skiing, and does not pretend to. It is an honest destination, often underrated, that deserves to be (re)discovered.

90bfc5c6b7aab868593262eaf0ea0d617e4ce207: A resort on a human scale, Astún focuses on the quality of its welcome and its closeness rather than impressive figures. Its 50 km of runs are ideal for a stay of 3 to 4 days, especially for families or skiers who do not need to constantly find new terrain. Technical terrain is king at Astún: with 17 black runs and 19 red runs on offer, confirmed skiers will find plenty to challenge them. Off-piste and freeride are practised here in often excellent conditions, thanks to the altitude and the orientation of the slopes. The altitude of Astún (1660 m at the base, 2300 m at the top) helps it keep decent snow through midwinter. January and February are the most reliable months; in December and March, it is worth checking conditions before finalising a booking. The budget for a stay at Astún is clearly high: 58€ for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants that are among the most expensive in the Alps. It is the price of excellence, but you should be aware of it before you go. In short, Astún keeps its promises. A Pyrenean resort that will suit most skiers without disappointing.
